description.summary: report the workspace a toplevel is on

protocol.description:
This protocol lets a privileged client learn which workspace each toplevel (as exposed by zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1) is on. It is meant to complement ext_workspace_v1.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is private to labwc and may change in incompatible ways.

interface.name: lab_toplevel_workspace_manager_v1
interface.description: This is a privileged global controlled by its own entry in the compositor's privileged-interface policy. It is only useful together with zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1 and ext_workspace_manager_v1.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. Existing lab_toplevel_workspace_v1 objects are not affected.

request.name: get_toplevel_workspace

description.summary: get the workspace object of a toplevel

request.description: Create a lab_toplevel_workspace_v1 object bound to the given toplevel for the lifetime of that toplevel. Immediately after creation the compositor sends workspace_enter for the workspace the toplevel is currently on.

interface.name: lab_toplevel_workspace_v1
interface.description:
Reports the workspace a toplevel is on.
Whenever the toplevel moves to another workspace, the compositor sends workspace_leave(old) followed by workspace_enter(new). A toplevel is on at most one workspace at a time, but the client must tolerate workspace_enter without a preceding workspace_leave (initial state) and workspace_leave without a following workspace_enter (the workspace is being destroyed, or the toplevel is going away).
The workspace_id is the same string the compositor sends in the id event of ext_workspace_handle_v1 for that workspace. The client matches it against the ids it received on its own ext_workspace_handle_v1 objects. A string is used instead of an object because a client may bind ext_workspace_manager_v1 several times and the compositor cannot know which binding the requester owns.
When the toplevel is closed, this object becomes inert: no more events are sent, but destroy still works. There is no closed event; the client learns about the closure from the zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1.
Destroying this object stops events; it never affects the toplevel.
No protocol errors are defined. Version 2 adds the move_to_workspace request.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Stop receiving events. This does not affect the toplevel.

event.name: workspace_enter
event.description: The toplevel is now on the workspace identified by workspace_id, which equals ext_workspace_handle_v1.id.

event.name: workspace_leave
event.description: The toplevel is no longer on the workspace identified by workspace_id, which equals ext_workspace_handle_v1.id.

request.name: move_to_workspace

description.summary: move the toplevel to a workspace

request.description: Ask the compositor to move the toplevel to the workspace identified by workspace_id (an ext_workspace_handle_v1.id). The compositor may ignore the request, e.g. if the workspace no longer exists or the toplevel is closed; it never sends a protocol error. On success the usual workspace_leave/workspace_enter events follow. The active workspace is not changed.
